problems.title: Passes over memory

parts.prompt: Three-kernel version (max; exp-sum writing exponentials; normalise): full-matrix reads + writes?
Fused single pass?
Fused time bound on a 512 GB/s GPU, in ms?

hints: Count every read and write of a matrix-sized array.
problems.solution: (a) Read (max), read + write (exp-sum), read + write (normalise): 5. (b) 2. (c) 128 MiB at 512 GB/s: 0.262 ms. 2.5× from fusion alone.

problems.title: Why subtract the max

parts.prompt: Largest x for which $e^x$ is finite in FP32 (to 1 decimal)?
Softmax of [1000, 1000] computed naively gives…

problems.solution: (a) 88.7. (b) $e^{1000}$ overflows to inf, and inf/inf is NaN. Subtracting the max makes the largest exponent $e^0 = 1$: no overflow, same result.

problems.title: Online softmax by hand
problems.statement: Process x = [2.0, 5.0, 1.0, 7.0] one at a time with the running pair (m, s), starting from (−∞, 0).

parts.prompt: Final m?
Final s (sum of $e^{x-m}$)?
Softmax of the 7?

hints: Each new element is the pair (x, 1).
problems.solution: m = 7, s = $e^{-5} + e^{-2} + e^{-6} + 1 = 1.1446$, and softmax(7) = $1/s = 0.8737$. The rescaling step $s e^{m_{old} - m}$ is what let the sum start before the max was known.

problems.title: Combining partial results
problems.statement: Two halves of a row have running pairs (m, s) = (3, 2.0) and (5, 1.5).

parts.prompt: Combined m?
Combined s?

hints: $(m_a, s_a) \oplus (m_b, s_b) = (m, s_a e^{m_a - m} + s_b e^{m_b - m})$.
problems.solution: m = 5, s = $2e^{-2} + 1.5 = 1.7707$. Because ⊕ is associative, the halves can come from different warps or blocks, in any tree.

problems.title: LayerNorm traffic
problems.statement: LayerNorm over rows of a 8192 × 4096 FP16 tensor with FP16 gamma/beta.

parts.prompt: Minimum DRAM bytes (read x once, write y once; ignore gamma/beta)?
Time bound at 1 TB/s, in µs?

hints: 2 bytes per element, read and write.
problems.solution: (a) 128 MiB. (b) 134 µs. A good LayerNorm kernel reaches 80–90% of this; anything near 50% is leaving 2× on the table.

problems.title: Variance, two ways

parts.prompt: Relative magnitude of the cancellation: $E[x^2]/\text{Var}$, roughly (order of magnitude)?
Which formula should a FP32 kernel use?
options: Two-pass (mean, then mean of squared deviations) or Welford

hints: $E[x^2] \approx 10^8$ while Var ≈ 0.67; FP32 keeps about 7 digits.
problems.solution: (a) $10^8 / 0.67 \approx 1.5 \times 10^8$: the subtraction must cancel 8 digits, more than FP32 has, so E[x²] − E[x]² is noise (numpy FP32 gives -8 here). (b) Two-pass from registers, or Welford's update, which never forms the huge squares.

problems.title: Fusing the residual
problems.statement: A transformer block computes h = x + attn(x), then y = LayerNorm(h), FP16, n elements.

parts.prompt: Bytes per element unfused (add kernel reads 2, writes 1; LayerNorm reads 1, writes 1)?
Fused add + LayerNorm (reads 2, writes y; h also written because the next residual needs it)?

problems.solution: (a) (3 + 2) × 2 = 10. (b) (2 + 2) × 2 = 8; if h isn't needed later, 6. Real transformer kernels fuse bias, residual and norm for exactly these savings.

problems.title: Block or warp per row

parts.prompt: Values per lane with one warp per row?
With one 256-thread block per row?
For rows of 65,536 values, prefer…
options: a warp per row, all in registers
a block per row, looping, or online softmax across chunks

problems.solution: 32 values per lane fit in registers; 65,536 per row would need 2,048 per lane. Long rows need a block per row (or several blocks with an online combine).

problems.title: Memory-bound means…
problems.statement: A fused GELU kernel runs at 85% of peak bandwidth.

parts.prompt: Replacing erff with a faster approximation will…
options: barely change it: memory sets the time

problems.solution: At 85% of bandwidth the math is hidden behind memory. Cheaper math matters only for compute- or issue-bound kernels.

problems.title: Reduced precision for memory-bound ops
problems.statement: An elementwise kernel over FP32 tensors runs at peak bandwidth.

parts.prompt: Speedup from storing the tensors in BF16 (computing in FP32)?

problems.solution: 2×: for memory-bound kernels, the storage type is the performance knob. Compute in FP32 registers, store narrow.
